content.overview: A company may close the register of Members, debenture-holders or other security holders for no more than forty-five days in aggregate in a year and no more than thirty days at one time. It must give at least seven days' prior notice, or the shorter period specified by SEBI for listed companies or companies intending to list, in the prescribed manner. Breach attracts a penalty of ₹5,000 per day while the register remains closed, capped at ₹1,00,000, on the company and every officer in default.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 91 (Power to close register of members or debenture-holders or other security holders). A company may close the register of Members, debenture-holders or other security holders for periods not exceeding forty-five days in aggregate in each year and not exceeding thirty days at any one time. Prior notice of at least seven days must be given in the prescribed manner, except that SEBI may specify a shorter period for listed companies or companies intending to get their securities listed. If the register is closed without the required notice, after shorter notice than permitted, or for a period exceeding either statutory limit, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty of ₹5,000 for every day during which the register is kept closed, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Permitted closure period
sections.body: A company may close the register of Members, debenture-holders or other security holders for periods not exceeding forty-five days in aggregate in each year and not exceeding thirty days at any one time.

sections.heading: Prior notice
sections.body: At least seven days' prior notice must be given in the prescribed manner. For listed companies or companies intending to get their securities listed, SEBI may specify a shorter notice period.

sections.heading: Default and penalty
sections.body: If the register is closed without the required notice, after shorter notice than permitted, or for a continuous or aggregate period exceeding the statutory limits, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty of ₹5,000 for every day during which the register is kept closed, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000.

hypotheticals.question: A company closes its register for thirty-one consecutive days after giving the required notice. What section 91 issue arises?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 91 permits no more than thirty days at any one time, even if the aggregate annual period remains below forty-five days. A closure exceeding that limit attracts the penalty stated in subsection (2).

hypotheticals.question: A listed company gives fewer than seven days' notice before closing its register. Is that automatically a breach?
hypotheticals.analysis: Check whether SEBI has specified a shorter notice period for listed companies or companies intending to list and whether the company followed the prescribed manner. The default seven-day period is subject to that statutory qualification.

distinctions.title: Annual aggregate and single-closure limits
distinctions.left: The register may be closed for no more than forty-five days in aggregate in a year.
distinctions.right: Each individual closure may not exceed thirty days at one time.

rows.left: At least seven days or a SEBI-specified shorter period
rows.right: Same notice rule applies to each closure

misconceptions.trap: Treating the forty-five-day annual aggregate as allowing more than thirty consecutive days.
misconceptions.correction: Both limits apply: no more than forty-five days in aggregate in a year and no more than thirty days at one time.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every company may use a shorter notice period without a SEBI specification.
misconceptions.correction: The shorter period exception is for listed companies or companies intending to list where SEBI specifies the shorter period.
The penalty is ₹5,000 per day while the register remains closed, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: A company may close the register of members or debenture holders for a total period not exceeding the statutory limit, on giving the prescribed notice.
